title: Knowledge Digester 1: the model, provenance and the absorption ledger
requested_outcome: Context: the Knowledge Digester (product memory SOURCE_ASSIMILATION_V1.md, NEXT_PHASE_2026-09-25.md section 2, and the owner's direction of 2026-09-26) is how CLIVE takes in any kind of external artifact - git repositories, agent skills, documents, API and tool specifications, datasets, web apps and themes, media, eventually any application or file - and turns it into provenance-tagged, reversible knowledge and capability. It lives in a new package, crooks-assistant/app/digest/, standard library only (no new dependencies), with no network access and no execution of anything it reads: digesting is reading. Build the digester's data model in app/digest/model.py and a small file store in app/digest/store.py, exported from app/digest/__init__.py. (1) Source: where an artifact came from - origin (URL or path as given), kind of origin (git, archive, file, directory, url, upload), pinned reference (commit SHA, content digest), licence as found, when it was taken in, and a content digest of the quarantined copy; an artifact never exists without its Source. (2) Artifact: one digested thing, with a deterministic id derived from its Source digest, its detected kinds (a list, since one repository can be a skill collection and a Python package at once) and its Units. (3) Unit: the smallest reusable piece, with a kind from a closed but extensible vocabulary - procedure (steps to do something), rule (a constraint or guideline), check (something testable), capability (something that can be called: a tool, endpoint or command), interface (a schema or contract), pattern (a reusable design or code shape), knowledge (a fact or explanation), data_schema, design_token, example, dependency, script (code that would run if executed - never run by the digester), claim (an assertion by the source that needs verifying) - plus title, a bounded text body, the exact location in the artifact (path and line span), a deterministic id, and tags. (4) Finding: something the digester noticed about safety or quality (for the scanner to fill), with severity, location and a plain explanation. (5) Absorption: a proposal or decision to use a Unit in CLIVE, with the target (builder skill, review check, tool or connector, product-memory knowledge, objective to build natively, reference only, rejected), the reasoning, who decided (proposed by CLIVE, decided by the owner), and the removal handle: every absorption records exactly what it added so it can be taken out again cleanly; nothing is absorbed without a way back. Everything is frozen dataclasses with to_dict/from_dict that round-trip exactly, and a JSON Schema for the serialised forms in app/digest/schema.py. The store writes one directory per artifact (source.json, artifact.json, units.jsonl, findings.jsonl, absorptions.jsonl) under a root it is given, refuses to overwrite a different artifact with the same id, and appends absorptions rather than rewriting them. Tests in tests/test_digest_model.py: deterministic ids, round-trips, schema validity of serialised examples (validate structurally with a small checker in the test, no new dependency), the store's refusal to overwrite and its append-only ledger, and that an Absorption without a removal handle is rejected. You cannot run commands: the loop runs the listed checks after you report and returns any failure output, and the independent review returns its findings, to your next attempt. Do not report an owner decision for GitHub acceptance: it runs automatically after your candidate is published.
acceptance_criteria: Source, Artifact, Unit, Finding and Absorption exist as frozen, round-tripping dataclasses with deterministic ids and a JSON Schema
the store keeps one directory per artifact, refuses conflicting overwrites and keeps absorptions append-only
every Absorption carries a removal handle and one without it is rejected
every listed check passes in the worker's workspace
